name: 14-dependency-uid-derivation
description: The issue_dependency uid field order, pinned against a value Tracker's live server produced. Authored by issuedb after measuring 16/16 agreement on the live feed; the expected uid was NOT computed by issuedb.

provenance.sample: 16 of 16 server-derived dependencies matched (project, blocker, blocked); 0 of 16 matched the reverse
provenance.caveat: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-22: the earlier note here claimed PROTOCOL.md did not specify this order. That was false when written and was asserted without reading the file. contracts/sync/PROTOCOL.md line 150 specifies `issue_dependency` = "idep", project_uid, blocker_uid, blocked_uid, committed 2026-08-15 (git blame 0fdcbabc) -- seven days before issuedb derived a dependency uid. This vector records what the counterpart actually produces, so a future divergence from the specified order is visible rather than silent.
provenance.specified_by: contracts/sync/PROTOCOL.md line 150, dated 2026-08-15, verified by direct read

cases.case: server-observed triple, endpoints are real project issues #2 and #3
cases.expected_uid_source: read from Tracker's pull feed, not computed by issuedb

cases.case: DISCRIMINATION: reversing the endpoints must NOT collide
cases.why: A dependency is directional. If this collided, A-blocks-B and B-blocks-A would be one row and a cycle would be unrepresentable. Pinning the POSITIVE value as well as the inequality makes the reversed order a cross-implementation pin too, not merely 'something else'.
cases.expected_uid_source: derived by Tracker's canonical.py and reported by tracker-manager-0e2462; confirmed equal to issuedb's derivation here. Not computed by issuedb alone.
